extracted.intended_audience: PCT applicants (inventors) and patent agents/attorneys filing national phase applications in Singapore
extracted.subtask_short: PCT national phase patent filing Singapore
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements and options for entering the Singapore national phase from a PCT international application, including deadlines, required documents, search/examination route choices, examination responses, review and grant procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: National phase entry — time limit and basic filing items
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application must be filed within 30 months.* and should include: Application form; Application fee: S$210/-; Singapore has been designated in the PCT International Application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: *From the declared priority date or where there is no declared priority date, from the date of filing of the PCT international application. The page notes a detailed flowchart is available. Failure to comply with the 30‑month national phase entry deadline will prevent entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement if PCT not in English
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PCT International Application was not filed in English, a translation of the international application into English and a verification of the translation must be enclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation and verification are required at national phase filing; ensure verified translation is included to avoid defects in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficiency notification and time to cure missing information
rubrics_metrics.description: If the necessary information is absent, the Registrar will notify you, who shall have 2 months from the date of the notification to provide what is lacking. Your application will be treated as withdrawn if you are unable to submit the necessary in time. Otherwise, a Date of Filing will be accorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond within the 2‑month cure period to avoid withdrawal; the Registrar issues the notification — timely cure preserves the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability criteria examined
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners will search for prior art and determine if the prior art destroys novelty. The patent examiner will also determine if the other patentability criteria (such as inventive step and industrial application) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty, inventive step (non‑obviousness), and industrial applicability are the core patentability standards to satisfy in Singapore examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of search and examination routes (Option 1/2/3)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can choose either of the 3 search and examination routes, depending on the availability of a foreign search and/or examination results and cost. Options differ by timeframe, fees, advantages and disadvantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options as described on the page: Option 1 — Search within 13 months + Examination within 36 months; Fees: Search (S$1,735) + Examination (S$1,420). Advantage: decide whether to proceed with examination depending on search results; Disadvantage: more expensive than Option 2 if proceeding to examination. Option 2 — Combined Search and Examination within 36 months; Fee: Combined (S$2,050). Advantage: time and cost savings vs Option 1. Option 3 — Examination within 36 months; Fee: Examination (S$1,420). Advantage: less expensive if a foreign search result is available; Disadvantage: there may be other prior arts not uncovered in earlier search. Fee discount and excess claim fees may apply for different options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign search/examination results and work‑sharing (PPH/ASPEC)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a foreign search and examination results from partnering offices, you can make use of working‑sharing arrangements such as Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) and ASEAN Patent Examination Cooperation (ASPEC) Programme to obtain a patent in Singapore faster and more efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where available, rely on foreign results to reduce time/cost; check eligibility for PPH/ASPEC and whether using foreign results fits your chosen route (e.g., Option 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination report outcomes and responses — deadlines and permitted responses
rubrics_metrics.description: After search and examination, an examination report or a supplementary examination report will be issued detailing the examiners’ opinion on registrability. If there are no unresolved objections: You will be issued a Notice of Eligibility to Proceed to Grant. If there are one or more unresolved objections: You are required to respond within 2 months (for simple amendments, i.e. invitation to amend) or 5 months (for written opinion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted responses to an invitation to amend: an amendment of the patent specification; or rejecting the invitation to amend. Permitted responses to a written opinion: written submissions on the patent examiner’s opinion; an amendment of the patent specification; rejection of the invitation to amend (with or without explanation); or both. Subsequent written opinion(s) may be issued until all outstanding issues are resolved. If issues cannot be resolved within 18 months from the date of the first written opinion, a Notice of Intention to Refuse will be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of unresolved issues — Notice of Intention to Refuse and response right
rubrics_metrics.description: If the outstanding issues cannot be resolved within 18 months from the date of the first written opinion, you will receive a Notice of Intention to Refuse from the Registry of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This triggers the opportunity to request further review (see Examination Review). Anticipate the 18‑month threshold and manage responses to avoid reaching the refusal stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Review after Notice of Intention to Refuse
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have received a Notice of Intention to Refuse, request for an Examination Review within 2 months from the date of the Notice of Intention to Refuse. If applicable, you may, at the same time, amend the specification of the patent application to overcome the unresolved objection(s). If you fail to request for an Examination Review, the patent application will be refused, and you will be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely request (within 2 months) is mandatory to avoid refusal; include any specification amendments when requesting review if they address the objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant stage — request for Certificate of Grant and consolidation following amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file a request for the issuance of the Certificate of Grant within 2 months after the issuance of the Notice of Eligibility to Proceed to Grant. If you have made any amendments or corrections to the original specification, you need to submit a set of consolidated specification together with the request for the issuance of the Certificate of Grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the request is filed and the conditions for grant are satisfied, the Registrar will issue the Certificate of Grant. If you fail to file the request, the patent application shall be treated as abandoned and the Registrar will notify you accordingly by letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees, fee discounts and excess claim fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Different search/examination options carry different fees (listed on the page) and a fee discount and excess claim fees may apply for the different options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the specific fee schedule and eligibility for discounts; account for excess claim fees (additional claims beyond a threshold) when budgeting for search/examination.
